The file viewer¶

The file viewer shows a raw IQ recording. This page tells you how wvt opens a file, and what each area of the window shows.

Open a file¶

Give the file on the command line, or type its path in the file row and click Open:

wvt recording.sigmf-meta

To open a saved session (the recording and the view, plots and channel that you saved), open the session file in the same way. Refer to File sessions.

Sample formats¶

wvt reads these sample formats. Add _be for big-endian samples, for example ci16_be.

Format

Sample

cf32

Complex 32-bit float

cf64

Complex 64-bit float

ci32

Complex 32-bit signed integer

ci16

Complex 16-bit signed integer

ci8

Complex 8-bit signed integer

cu8

Complex 8-bit unsigned integer (RTL-SDR)

How wvt finds the file settings¶

wvt gets the sample format, the sample rate and the center frequency from these sources, in this order:

  1. SigMF .sigmf-meta and .sigmf-data files.

  2. gqrx file names, for example gqrx_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<fc>_<rate>_fc.raw.

  3. Values in the file name, for example 2.4MSps or 915MHz.

  4. The file extension, for example .cu8, .cs8, .cs16, .cf32, .cfile or .raw.

wvt reads the SigMF core:datatype from global, and core:sample_rate, core:frequency and core:datetime from global or the first capture. The datatype must be a complex type in the table above (_le or _be). wvt does not open a SigMF file with a different datatype (for example ri16_le, real samples), because it would show noise. To read the file with a different format, give -f. If the metadata has no datatype, wvt reads the file as cf32 and shows a warning.

The command-line options override all the values that wvt finds:

Option

Value

-f, --format FMT

The sample format

-r, --rate HZ

The sample rate. SI suffixes are permitted, for example 2.4M

-c, --fc HZ

The center frequency

-H, --header BYTES

The number of bytes to skip at the start of the file

--swap-iq

Swap I and Q

While the file is open, you can change each value in the file row. The Format drop-down has the sample format, the I/Q swap, the byte order and the header size.

Large files¶

wvt memory-maps the file. Thus wvt can open files that are larger than the memory of the computer. For files that are very large, load a part of the file only. Refer to Load a segment.

wvt does not support a file that a different program is still writing. If the file gets shorter while it is open (for example, a recorder that starts the file again), the part after the new end shows as zeros, and the status bar shows a warning. To see the new length, open the file again.

Screen layout¶

Area

Contents

Menu bar

The File, View, Tools and Help menus. Refer to Menus. On the right: TX ON, REC, a running audio or export, and the Source (File or Device)

File row

The file path, Format, sample rate, center frequency, segment (start and end time to load), and file size

Navigation row

Buttons to go to the start or the end, and to move back or forward by 10 % or by one page. Zoom in, zoom out and zoom all. The span presets, the span and the start time. Go to has a sample index, Add bookmark and the bookmarks

Overview strip

The power over the full file or segment. The white box is the current view. Drag the box to move the view. Drag its edges to change the view size. Click a different point to go there. You can hide the strip in the View menu. wvt also hides it when the window is short

Scrollbar

Moves the view through the file. Drag the thumb, click the track to move one page, or turn the mouse wheel

Left

The waterfall settings: FFT size, window, dB range or auto. The ⚙ button has the overlap, averaging, rows, columns, colormap and peak hold. Below the settings are the spectrum of the current view, the waterfall, and its color bar

Right

The channel settings: on or off, offset, bandwidth, and to peak. The ⚙ button has the taps, decimation, squelch, maximum points and plot height. Below the settings are the I/Q, AM, FM and PM plots, which you can scroll. Each plot header has a show checkbox, a ⚙ button for the plot options, and the measurement readout. Thus no text covers the traces

Status bar

The Snapshot… button (refer to Plot snapshots). The values at the pointer: time, sample number, frequency, dB, AM, FM and PM. The marker ΔT, 1/ΔT and ΔF, and the point markers (P2 minus P1). GPU <model> or CPU, the renderer, and computing... NN% while wvt calculates the plots (the percentage done)

Menus¶

Menu

Items

File

Open file, export region, save plot snapshots, save file session (refer to File sessions), quit

View

Time markers, frequency markers, point markers, relative frequency, peak hold, the overview strip, the time plots to show, show everything

Tools

Signal generator, audio, use the GPU

Help

Keyboard and mouse, about wvt

Linked views¶

  • All time axes have one range: the vertical axis of the waterfall and the horizontal axis of each plot on the right.

  • The spectrum and the waterfall have one frequency range.

  • When the pointer is on a plot, all the other plots show a crosshair at the same time or frequency.

  • The time markers (T1 and T2) show in all plots. You can drag them in each plot. Press Z to zoom to the span between them.

The spectrum of the view¶

The spectrum above the waterfall shows the average and the peak hold of all the waterfall rows in the view. When you pan or zoom, wvt calculates the spectrum again. For the calculation, refer to Signal processing.

The channel filter and the time plots¶

The channel filter selects one signal for the I/Q, AM, FM and PM plots.

  • To enable the filter, press C, or tick Channel in the channel settings.

  • To tune the channel, Ctrl+click the spectrum or the waterfall.

  • To move the channel, drag its center line (cyan). To change the bandwidth, drag an edge line.

  • To peak puts the channel on the strongest signal in the visible spectrum.

To start with the filter on, use --chan OFFSET:BW, for example --chan 300k:150k. To start with a time range, use --view T0:T1, for example --view 0.5:0.52.

Each time plot has options. To see them, click its ⚙ button, or right-click the plot. For the calculations, refer to Signal processing.

Bookmarks and markers¶

  • Press B to add a bookmark at the view. Go to shows the bookmarks.

  • Press T to show or hide the time markers. Press F to show or hide the frequency markers.

  • The status bar shows the time between the markers (ΔT), its inverse (1/ΔT) and the frequency difference (ΔF).

Point measurements¶

Two point markers, P1 and P2, measure between two points of the signal. For example, the time between two pulse edges, the time between two pulses, or the change in frequency in a pulse.

  • To put a marker at the pointer, press M or Alt+click a plot: the waterfall, the spectrum, I/Q, AM, FM or PM. The first marker is P1 and the second is P2. After that, each new marker replaces the older of the two.

  • On a time plot (I/Q, AM, FM, PM), the marker goes on the trace. If a peak or a valley is less than 8 pixels to the side and nearer to the pointer, the marker goes there. Thus, put the pointer a little above the top of a pulse to put the marker on the top. On the I/Q plot, the marker goes on the trace (I or Q) that is nearer to the pointer.

  • On the waterfall, the marker keeps the time and the frequency of the pointer. On the spectrum, it keeps the frequency.

  • To move a marker, drag it. On a time plot, it moves along the trace.

  • To remove the markers, press Shift+M, or use View → Clear point markers. View → Point markers shows or hides them.

The status bar shows P2 minus P1 for each value that the two markers have in common. The label at P2 shows the same values:

P1 and P2 on

Differences

The same time plot

dT (with 1/dT and the number of samples) and the value (for example dAM, dFM in Hz, dPM in rad or deg)

I and Q

dT and the amplitude (dA)

Two different time plots, or a time plot and the waterfall

dT

The waterfall

dT, dF and the power (dP, dB)

The spectrum

dF and the power (dP, dB)

The spectrum and the waterfall

dF

The time axis and the frequency axis are shared by the plots, so dT and dF are correct between two plots. The other plots show each marker as a faint line at its time or frequency.

A value comes from the plotted data. When a marker on a time plot goes out of the view, wvt keeps its last value until a plot setting changes. A value that wvt does not know shows as ?: zoom or pan to the marker. In a sparse view (refer to the channel options), zoom in for exact values.

Point markers are not available in live mode.
